title: Crisis, country, and party lines: politicians' misinformation behavior and public engagement
screen_reason: Observational study of 3,277 politicians' tweets (2020-2021) in Germany, Italy, the UK and the USA. All shared URLs were expanded and matched to the NewsGuard domain rating database; domains scoring below 60 were classified as misinformation. Table 1 reports, per country, the number of misinformation tweets and the total number of matched (mis)information tweets, giving a share of shared news links that are untrustworthy. This is SHARING (content_share) with a behavioural denominator.

estimates.measure_type: % of German politicians' tweeted news-domain links that came from a NewsGuard-untrustworthy domain
estimates.denominator: 68,871 tweets by 765 German national-executive, national-legislative and regional-executive politicians that contained a URL matched to the NewsGuard database
estimates.definition: The tweet linked to a news domain whose NewsGuard trust score was below 60
estimates.misinfo_def: "misinformation, broadly defined as any information that is misleading, unreliable, and/or turns out to be false"
estimates.ground_truth_detail: NewsGuard website credibility ratings (nine credibility/transparency criteria, score out of 100); domains scoring < 60 coded misinformation. No inter-coder reliability applicable; the COVID/non-COVID classifier reached F1 0.83-0.92.
estimates.moderator_quote: Domains with a score below 60 are considered misinformation.
estimates.notes: Value computed as an exact part/whole from the two verbatim counts in Table 1 (misinformation tweets over total matched tweets), which sum exactly to the reported total. The percentages printed in Table 1's parentheses are each country's share of the four-country total, not the misinformation share. Data collection spans 2020-2021; year coded as the end of the window.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted, deliberately: (a) the four-country pooled figure (11,062 / 411,347 = 2.69%), because it is the sum of the four country rows already coded and would double count; (b) the per-politician mean misinformation ratios (Italy M = 0.049, SD = 0.147; USA M = 0.022; Germany M = 0.011; UK M = 0.004) - these are means of individual-level ratios, not a share of items, and the item-level Table 1 counts give the same quantity more cleanly; (c) the party-level shares, which are subgroup breakdowns within the country cells already coded: AfD 8.2% (n = 951), Die Linke 0.2% (n = 23), CDU/CSU 0.1% (n = 7) in Germany; FdI 41.7% (n = 2,747), Gruppo Misto 9.7% (n = 1,846), Lega 9.2% (n = 927) in Italy; Conservative 0.5% (n = 149), Labour 0.1% (n = 59) in the UK; Republicans 4.6% (n = 2,501), Democrats 1.0% (n = 774) in the USA. Party is a headline of RQ4, so these could defensibly be added as subgroup rows; they are recorded here instead to keep one prevalence estimate per country x platform cell. Also not extracted: the share of misinformation attributed to each party (AfD 95.5%, FdI 70.7%, Conservative 57.3%, Republican 76.4%) - these are shares of the misinformation set, not prevalence; the regional-executive shares (USA 11.1%, UK 6.8%), which have no stated denominator; and all engagement beta coefficients (e.g. USA misinformation drew 2.55 times the average engagement of reliable information), which are engagement ratios, not prevalence shares.

rob.design: Politicians systematically sampled from official government/parliament websites in DE, IT, UK, US (national executive, national legislative, regional executive; 3,277 accounts after excluding accounts inactive in 2020-2021), with all their 2020-2021 tweets retrieved via the Twitter Academic API. 1,771,518 URLs collected, 411,347 matched to NewsGuard. Misinformation coded at domain level (NewsGuard < 60), so no inter-coder reliability; the auxiliary COVID/non-COVID classifier was validated against manually coded test sets with F1 0.83-0.92. Authors note the source-based approach cannot capture misinformation in politicians' own original text, and that linking to a low-rated domain need not mean the tweet is misleading.
rob.item6_quote: The processed domain lists were then matched against the NewsGuard rating database [40], a third-party independent resource for news domain credibility.
rob.item10_quote: We collected and processed a total of 1,771,518 URLs, of which 411,347 matched with the NewsGuard database as containing a link to an external news domain.
